correctness.rationale: For p,q>=3 and k>=0, the universal cover is a subdivided 3-regular branch tree with incident thread lengths (p,p,k+1) at a left branch and (q,q,k+1) at a right branch. Lemma 2.6 of Krebs–Verbitsky uses the same uniform round-zero convention. When p<q, no outgoing branch-degree discrepancy is visible before depth p+1; at that depth the two p-threads distinguish the left root, while the connector is identical at both roots. Stable branch types and the distances to the first branch in the two directions separate the three regions when p!=q. Reflection gives precisely the remaining cycle orbits. When p=q, reversal exchanges the branches and unordered endpoint distances classify each thread; distinct sums separate connector and cycles unless k+1=p=q. In that balanced case the branch tree is uniformly subdivided and corresponding positions are color-equivalent, while cut-vertex status prevents a cycle/connector automorphism. The finite replay confirms 13056 triples and 12240 split times, but does not replace the uniform proof.
residual_risks: The finite replay is bounded to 3<=p,q<=18 and 0<=k<=50; the all-parameter conclusion relies on the universal-cover argument.

value.rationale: Dumbbells form a standard connected bicyclic family immediately beyond the tree/unicyclic regime. The theorem gives a complete boundary for failure of color refinement to recover automorphism orbits: exactly equal cycle and connector lengths. It closes the unequal-cycle domain that the prior resonance calculation left open, including connectors whose length equals just one of the two cycles. The exact split time explains how the cycle-length asymmetry becomes observable. This is a motivated structural classification, rather than a numerical improvement or a generic claim of significance.
residual_risks: No classification of amenability, arbitrary cactus graphs or higher-dimensional Weisfeiler–Leman is claimed.
